hypotheses.justification: The statement elaborates and is true without `[Finite ι]`. `DifferentiableOn 𝕜 c s` is defined in the TVS section of `FDeriv/Defs.lean`, which needs only AddCommGroup, Module and TopologicalSpace on the codomain. The topology on `ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 M H` (`ContinuousMultilinearMap.instTopologicalSpace`, in `Topology/Algebra/Module/Multilinear/Topology.lean`) needs no finiteness of `ι`. The `NormedAddCommGroup` instance needs `Fintype ι`, which `[Finite ι]` does not provide, so the statement already uses the general topological instance. The map `ContinuousMultilinearMap.apply 𝕜 M H u` is a continuous linear map for any `ι`. Proof without the hypothesis: for `x ∈ s`, take `c'` with `HasFDerivWithinAt c c' s x`, and let `g := ContinuousMultilinearMap.apply 𝕜 M H u`. Then `(c y) u - (c x) u - (g ∘L c') (y - x) = g (c y - c x - c' (y - x))`. By `ContinuousLinearMap.isBigOTVS_comp` (the same step used in `HasFDerivAtFilter.comp`) this is `=O` of `c y - c x - c' (y - x)`, which is `=o` of `y - x` by `hasFDerivWithinAt_iff_isLittleOTVS`. So `g ∘L c'` is the derivative of `fun y ↦ (c y) u` within `s` at `x`. The existing proof goes through `HasFDerivWithinAt.continuousMultilinear_apply_const`, which takes `[Fintype ι]`, and through `HasFDerivWithinAt.comp`, which takes a normed middle space, so the proof would have to redo the `isLittleOTVS` argument by hand. No degenerate case (empty `ι`, empty `s`) breaks it. I could not run Lean, so I did not check that the hand-written proof compiles.
